```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(pheatmap)
library(DT)
library(knitr)

VELOCITY_DIR       <- file.path("output/objects/cellrank/cytotrace_res1_5")
CELLRANK_TABLE_DIR <- file.path(VELOCITY_DIR, "tables")
CELLRANK_FIG_DIR   <- file.path(VELOCITY_DIR, "figures")
CLUSTER_COL        <- "sNN_pca.SCT_30_res.1.5"
TARGET_CLUSTER     <- "1"
```

## Overview

CellRank trajectory inference on the HSC compartment (50,056 cells) using
**CytoTRACE2 score** as the pseudotime proxy. CytoTRACE2 reflects
transcriptional complexity: higher scores indicate more stem-like, less
differentiated states. The `PseudotimeKernel` translates these scores into
directed transition probabilities that guide cells from progenitor to terminal
fates.

**Workflow summary**

| Step | Method | Output |
|------|--------|--------|
| Pseudotime | CytoTRACE2 score (pre-computed) | `cytotrace2_score` in obs |
| Transition matrix | `PseudotimeKernel` (0.8) + `ConnectivityKernel` (0.2) | directed graph |
| Terminal states | CFLARE — sparse eigendecomposition | 14 macrostates |
| Fate probabilities | Linear system per terminal state | per-cell fate scores |
| Driver genes | Fate–expression correlation per cluster | ranked gene lists |
| Gene trends | GAM along pseudotime | expression curves |

> **Cluster column:** `sNN_pca.SCT_30_res.1.5` (33 clusters). Terminal state
> names encode the dominant cluster label at **res 0.9** (used during the
> CellRank Python run); per-cluster statistics in sections 5 and 8 are
> computed at res 1.5.

---

## 1  CytoTRACE2 pseudotime

```{r cytotrace-umap, fig.cap="Left: CytoTRACE2 score (RdYlBu_r, high = stem-like). Right: cluster labels at res 0.9 (used for terminal-state naming).", out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(CELLRANK_FIG_DIR, "overview_umap.png"))
```

**Interpretation.** CytoTRACE2 score reflects transcriptional complexity:
cells expressing more unique genes score higher and are inferred to be more
primitive. A gradient from high-scoring progenitor regions to lower-scoring,
more committed regions is expected across the UMAP. The right panel shows
the res 0.9 cluster structure used to name terminal states (e.g. `7_1`
= first CFLARE state dominated by cluster 7 at res 0.9).

> **Direction note.** `PseudotimeKernel` directs transitions toward *higher*
> pseudotime values. CytoTRACE2 is high = stem-like, so terminal states
> correspond to the most primitive progenitor attractors — not committed
> endpoints. To model forward differentiation, invert:
> `cytotrace2_pseudotime = 1 − cytotrace2_score`.

---

## 2  Kernel projection — directed transitions

```{r kernel-projection, fig.cap="Transition probability arrows projected onto UMAP. Arrow direction reflects the inferred differentiation flow derived from CytoTRACE2 pseudotime.", out.width="90%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(CELLRANK_FIG_DIR, "kernel_projection.png"))
```

**Interpretation.** Each arrow summarises the net expected displacement of a
cell under the transition matrix.

- **PseudotimeKernel (80%)** — biases transitions towards cells with higher
  CytoTRACE2 score (i.e., towards more stem-like states under uninverted score).
- **ConnectivityKernel (20%)** — local neighbourhood smoothing, preventing
  sharp directional discontinuities.

Coherent arrow streams indicate genuine directional flow; disordered arrows
in a region suggest either progenitor plasticity or ambiguous pseudotime
ordering there.

---

## 3  CFLARE eigenspectrum

```{r cflare-spectrum, fig.cap="Real part of the leading eigenvalues of the transition matrix. The eigenvalue gap indicates the number of quasi-stable macrostates.", out.width="70%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(CELLRANK_FIG_DIR, "cflare_spectrum.png"))
```

**Interpretation.** Eigenvalues near 1 correspond to absorbing or
near-absorbing states — populations where trajectories tend to end. CFLARE
(`k = 6` eigenvectors, 14 predicted states) is used instead of GPCCA because
the dense Schur decomposition at 50k cells requires ~23 GB. The spectrum can
be used to revisit the `k` choice: a visible gap after the retained eigenvalues
validates it.

---

## 4  Terminal states

```{r terminal-states, fig.cap="CFLARE terminal states on UMAP. 14 macrostates identified; names encode dominant res-0.9 cluster label.", out.width="90%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(CELLRANK_FIG_DIR, "terminal_states.png"))
```

**Interpretation.** CFLARE identified **14 terminal states** from `k = 6`
eigenvectors. State names (e.g., `5_1`, `3_2`) encode the dominant cluster
label at res 0.9 followed by a counter for states sharing that cluster.
Biologically, each terminal state represents a transcriptional attractor:
expected attractors include megakaryocyte progenitors, erythroid progenitors,
and lymphoid/myeloid-committed populations.

---

## 5  Fate probabilities

```{r fate-probs-umap, fig.cap="Per-cell fate probability for each of the 14 terminal states on UMAP. Probabilities sum to 1 per cell.", out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(CELLRANK_FIG_DIR, "fate_probabilities.png"))
```

**Interpretation.** Cells committed to a single fate show probability ≈ 1 for
that state. Multipotent progenitors distribute probability across several fates.
Cross-referencing with known lineage markers (`Gata1` for erythroid,
`Pf4`/`Vwf` for MK, `Csf1r` for myeloid) annotates each macrostate.

### 5.1  Mean fate probability per cluster (res 1.5)

```{r fate-per-cluster}
fp <- read.csv(file.path(CELLRANK_TABLE_DIR, "fate_prob_per_cluster.csv"),
               check.names = FALSE)
colnames(fp)[1] <- "cluster"
fp$cluster <- as.character(fp$cluster)

fp_round <- fp
fp_round[, -1] <- round(fp[, -1], 3)

DT::datatable(
  fp_round,
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption  = "Mean fate probability per cluster (rows) at res 1.5 for each CytoTRACE2 terminal state (columns).",
  options  = list(scrollX = TRUE, pageLength = 15, dom = "ft")
) |>
  DT::formatStyle(
    columns          = colnames(fp_round)[-1],
    background       = DT::styleColorBar(c(0, 1), "#b8d4e8"),
    backgroundSize   = "90% 70%",
    backgroundRepeat = "no-repeat",
    backgroundPosition = "center"
  )
```

```{r fate-heatmap, fig.height=8, fig.width=12, fig.cap="Heatmap of mean fate probability per cluster at res 1.5. Rows = clusters, columns = terminal states."}
mat <- as.matrix(fp[, -1])
rownames(mat) <- fp$cluster
mat_scaled <- apply(mat, 2, function(x) (x - min(x)) / (max(x) - min(x) + 1e-9))

pheatmap(
  mat_scaled,
  color           = colorRampPalette(c("white", "#2166ac"))(100),
  cluster_rows    = TRUE,
  cluster_cols    = TRUE,
  display_numbers = round(mat, 2),
  number_color    = "black",
  fontsize_number = 5,
  fontsize_row    = 8,
  fontsize_col    = 8,
  angle_col       = 45,
  main            = "Mean fate probability per cluster — res 1.5 (CytoTRACE2)\n(colour = column-scaled; numbers = raw probability)"
)
```

### 5.2  Fate probabilities by condition

```{r fate-by-condition, fig.cap="Fate probability distributions per terminal state split by sample. Shifts between WT, Het mCh−, and Het mCh+ indicate condition-specific lineage biases.", out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(CELLRANK_FIG_DIR, "fate_by_condition.png"))
```

## 6  Lineage driver genes

```{r lineage-drivers, results="asis"}
driver_dir  <- file.path(CELLRANK_FIG_DIR, "lineage_drivers")
driver_pngs <- sort(list.files(driver_dir, pattern = "\\.png$", full.names = TRUE))

for (png in driver_pngs) {
  ts_name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(png))
  cat(sprintf("\n### Terminal state: %s\n\n", ts_name))
  cat(sprintf('<img src="%s" style="width:90%%;display:block;margin:auto;">\n\n',
              xfun::base64_uri(png)))
}
```

**Interpretation.** Driver genes have the highest correlation between
expression level and the probability of reaching a given terminal state.

| Marker | Lineage |
|--------|---------|
| `Gata1`, `Klf1` | Erythroid |
| `Pf4`, `Vwf`, `Mpl` | Megakaryocyte |
| `Mpo`, `Csf1r` | Myeloid / monocyte |
| `Cd34`, `Kit`, `Slamf1` | Progenitor |

## 7  Gene expression trends along pseudotime

```{r gene-trends, fig.cap="GAM-smoothed expression of canonical HSC and lineage marker genes along CytoTRACE2 pseudotime, per terminal state.", out.width="100%", fig.height=14}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(CELLRANK_FIG_DIR, "gene_trends.png"))
```

**Interpretation.** Each panel shows how expression changes as cells progress
along the pseudotime axis towards each terminal fate. Divergent trends between
terminal states confirm that CellRank has resolved distinct lineage trajectories.

## 8  Cluster-level transition matrix (res 1.5)

The cluster × cluster transition matrix $T^{cl}$ is aggregated from the
full-resolution sparse Markov matrix and row-normalised. Entry $T^{cl}_{ij}$
is the expected fraction of outgoing flux from cluster $i$ that reaches cluster
$j$ in one step. Values computed at **res 1.5** (33 clusters).

```{r cl-trans-table}
cl_trans <- read.csv(file.path(CELLRANK_TABLE_DIR, "cluster_transition_matrix.csv"),
                     check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)

DT::datatable(
  round(cl_trans, 3),
  caption = "Cluster × cluster one-step Markov transition probabilities — res 1.5 (rows sum to 1). CytoTRACE2 kernel.",
  options = list(scrollX = TRUE, pageLength = 15, dom = "ft")
) |>
  DT::formatStyle(
    columns          = colnames(cl_trans),
    background       = DT::styleColorBar(c(0, 1), "#fed976"),
    backgroundSize   = "90% 70%",
    backgroundRepeat = "no-repeat",
    backgroundPosition = "center"
  )
```

```{r cl-trans-heatmap, fig.height=10, fig.width=10, fig.cap="Cluster transition probability heatmap — res 1.5 (CytoTRACE2). High diagonal = terminal/slow clusters; high off-diagonal = directed flux."}
mat_plot <- as.matrix(cl_trans)
cl_order <- tryCatch(
  as.character(sort(as.numeric(rownames(mat_plot)))),
  error = function(e) rownames(mat_plot)
)
mat_plot <- mat_plot[cl_order, cl_order]

breaks <- c(seq(0, 0.1, length.out = 90), seq(0.1, 1.0, length.out = 11))
breaks <- sort(unique(breaks))

pheatmap(
  mat_plot,
  color           = colorRampPalette(c("#f7f7f7", "#fed976", "#b10026"))(length(breaks) - 1),
  breaks          = breaks,
  cluster_rows    = FALSE,
  cluster_cols    = FALSE,
  display_numbers = round(mat_plot, 2),
  number_color    = "black",
  fontsize_number = 4,
  fontsize_row    = 8,
  fontsize_col    = 8,
  angle_col       = 45,
  main            = "CellRank cluster transition probabilities — res 1.5 (CytoTRACE2)\nRows sum to 1"
)
```

## 9  Cluster 1 fate analysis

Cluster 1 (at res 1.5) is examined as a potential intermediate or progenitor
state. This section (a) profiles the fate probability distribution for cluster 1
cells, (b) identifies clusters that send the greatest Markov flux *into* cluster
1 (candidate clusters of origin), and (c) compares fate profiles of candidate
origin clusters with cluster 1.

### 9.1  Fate probability profile of cluster 1

```{r c1-fate-profile, fig.height=5, fig.width=9, fig.cap="Mean fate probability for cluster 1 cells across all 14 CytoTRACE2 terminal states."}
fp1 <- fp |>
  filter(cluster == TARGET_CLUSTER) |>
  select(-cluster) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "terminal_state", values_to = "mean_prob") |>
  arrange(desc(mean_prob))

ggplot(fp1, aes(x = reorder(terminal_state, -mean_prob), y = mean_prob)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2166ac", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(mean_prob, 3)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  labs(
    title    = paste0("Cluster ", TARGET_CLUSTER, " — Mean fate probability (CytoTRACE2)"),
    x        = "Terminal state",
    y        = "Mean fate probability",
    caption  = "Cluster resolution: sNN_pca.SCT_30_res.1.5"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r c1-fate-table}
DT::datatable(
  fp1 |> mutate(mean_prob = round(mean_prob, 4)),
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption  = paste0("Cluster ", TARGET_CLUSTER, " fate probabilities, ranked by mean probability."),
  options  = list(pageLength = 20, dom = "t")
)
```

### 9.2  Candidate clusters of origin

Clusters that send the most Markov flux into cluster 1 are the most likely
progenitor sources. The column of the transition matrix for cluster 1
($T^{cl}_{i,1}$) gives the per-step probability of transitioning from cluster
$i$ to cluster 1.

```{r c1-origin-candidates, fig.height=5, fig.width=9, fig.cap="Inbound Markov flux into cluster 1 from all other clusters. Bars ranked by transition probability."}
cl_trans_sorted <- cl_trans[
  tryCatch(as.character(sort(as.numeric(rownames(cl_trans)))), error = function(e) rownames(cl_trans)),
  , drop = FALSE
]

inbound <- data.frame(
  source_cluster = rownames(cl_trans_sorted),
  prob_to_c1     = cl_trans_sorted[, TARGET_CLUSTER]
) |>
  filter(source_cluster != TARGET_CLUSTER) |>
  arrange(desc(prob_to_c1))

TOP_N <- 10
top_origins <- inbound |> slice_head(n = TOP_N)

ggplot(top_origins,
       aes(x = reorder(source_cluster, -prob_to_c1), y = prob_to_c1)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#d6604d", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(prob_to_c1, 3)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  labs(
    title   = paste0("Top ", TOP_N, " candidate origin clusters for cluster ", TARGET_CLUSTER,
                     " (CytoTRACE2)"),
    x       = "Source cluster",
    y       = paste0("P(source → cluster ", TARGET_CLUSTER, ") per Markov step"),
    caption = "Cluster resolution: sNN_pca.SCT_30_res.1.5"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r c1-origin-table}
DT::datatable(
  inbound |> mutate(prob_to_c1 = round(prob_to_c1, 4)),
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption  = paste0("All clusters ranked by Markov flux into cluster ", TARGET_CLUSTER, "."),
  options  = list(pageLength = 15, dom = "ft")
)
```

### 9.3  Fate comparison: origin clusters vs cluster 1

Rows below compare the mean fate probability profile of cluster 1 against
the top origin clusters identified above, revealing whether the origin
populations share or diverge from cluster 1's fate landscape.

```{r c1-fate-comparison, fig.height=7, fig.width=12, fig.cap="Mean fate probability heatmap for cluster 1 and its top candidate origin clusters. Colour = column-scaled probability; numbers = raw values."}
origin_clusters <- top_origins$source_cluster[seq_len(min(8, nrow(top_origins)))]
show_clusters   <- c(origin_clusters, TARGET_CLUSTER)

fp_subset <- fp |>
  filter(cluster %in% show_clusters) |>
  mutate(cluster = factor(cluster, levels = show_clusters))

mat_sub <- as.matrix(fp_subset[, -1])
rownames(mat_sub) <- fp_subset$cluster

mat_sub_scaled <- apply(mat_sub, 2, function(x) (x - min(x)) / (max(x) - min(x) + 1e-9))

# Highlight cluster 1 row
row_ann <- data.frame(
  type = ifelse(rownames(mat_sub) == TARGET_CLUSTER, "Target (cluster 1)", "Origin candidate"),
  row.names = rownames(mat_sub)
)
ann_colors <- list(type = c("Target (cluster 1)" = "#d6604d", "Origin candidate" = "#92c5de"))

pheatmap(
  mat_sub_scaled,
  color            = colorRampPalette(c("white", "#2166ac"))(100),
  cluster_rows     = FALSE,
  cluster_cols     = TRUE,
  annotation_row   = row_ann,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors,
  display_numbers  = round(mat_sub, 3),
  number_color     = "black",
  fontsize_number  = 6,
  fontsize_row     = 10,
  fontsize_col     = 9,
  angle_col        = 45,
  main             = paste0("Fate profiles: cluster ", TARGET_CLUSTER,
                            " vs candidate origin clusters (CytoTRACE2)\n",
                            "(colour = column-scaled; numbers = raw probability)")
)
```

## Methods

### How CellRank works

CellRank frames trajectory inference as a **finite, absorbing Markov chain**.
The transition matrix $T$ encodes the probability of moving from cell $i$ to
cell $j$ in one step, constructed from:

**`PseudotimeKernel`** — assigns transition weights using a sigmoid:

$$w_{ij} = \sigma\!\left(\nu \cdot \frac{t_j - t_i}{\text{std}(t)}\right)$$

where $t$ is the pseudotime variable. High-$t$ neighbours are favoured;
low-$t$ neighbours are penalised.

**`ConnectivityKernel`** — symmetrised $k$-NN graph; adds smoothing only
(undirected). Combined at 80:20 ratio.

**CFLARE** identifies terminal states from the top $k$ eigenvectors of $T$
(eigenvalues near 1 = near-absorbing states). Fate probabilities are solved
from the linear system $(I - Q)\Pi = R$ per terminal state using GMRES + ILU.

### CytoTRACE2 as pseudotime

CytoTRACE2 scores cells on transcriptional complexity. It is a *potency* score,
not a *trajectory* score — it has no knowledge of the specific differentiation
graph. In the current run, higher CytoTRACE2 = higher pseudotime, so terminal
states correspond to the most primitive progenitor attractors. Inverting
(`1 − score`) would produce forward-differentiation terminal states.

### Cluster transition matrix (res 1.5)

The cluster-level matrix $T^{cl}_{ij}$ is derived by row-normalised aggregation
over the full-resolution cell-level sparse matrix:

$$T^{cl}_{ij} = \frac{1}{n_i} \sum_{a \in C_i} \sum_{b \in C_j} T_{ab}$$

Computed at res 1.5 (33 clusters) from the stored `transition_matrix.npz`.
